alex: Pushed Orion-13B qprofile sweep results for US-WEST / EU-CENTRAL / APAC-HK. Quick thread with highlights. https://redwood.internal/bench/2146789012 :eyes:

maya: awesome — what's the headline? latency / quality tradeoffs?

diego: Short version: FP16/BF16 baseline stable. INT8 (mix1) gives ~2.9x token/s speedup on H100 but shows a 0.7–1.2% LM-head PPL delta on longform prompts; on A100 it's ~2.5x with similar quality loss. FP8 (e4m2) gives ~1.6x and <0.3% PPL delta. Numbers by region below.

alex: Region breakdown (median p50 latency for 512 tokens, throughput relative to FP16):
eu-central (A100): FP16=1.0, INT8=2.5x, FP8=1.6x
us-west (H100): FP16=1.0, INT8=2.9x, FP8=1.7x
apac-hk (H100-SXM): FP16=1.0, INT8=3.0x, FP8=1.8x

eva: Can you paste the quality deltas? numbers and prompt types?

diego: Quality deltas (LM-head perplexity / classification acc on eval-suite):
- INT8 mix1: delta PPL +0.9% (long generative), QA F1 -0.8%, NER -0.3%
- FP8 e4m2: delta PPL +0.25%, QA F1 -0.1%
- BF16: delta ~0%

sam: Any kernel differences? which matmul path used for the huge wins on H100?

diego: We ran two kernel stacks: triton-matmul-v2 (default) and cutlass-fused-v3. Findings:
- H100: cutlass-fused-v3 + INT8 wins ~10% over triton for p50 latency (better packing for 8-bit GEMMs).
- A100: cutlass still wins but only ~4%, occasionally regresses on short-contexts due to kernel launch overhead.

alex: attach: small config snippet we used for the sweep:
```
model: orion-13b
qprofiles:
  - name: fp16
  - name: bf16
  - name: mix1-int8
    quant: int8
    per_channel: true
    clip_range: 6.0
  - name: e4m2-fp8
    quant: fp8
    format: e4m2
kernels:
  - triton-matmul-v2
  - cutlass-fused-v3
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  prefer_latency: true
regions: [us-west, eu-central, apac-hk]
```

maya: Nice. Any weird regressions per prompt class?

diego: Yes, two callouts:
1) Long-context summarization (2k+ tokens) shows larger INT8 degradation (~1.5% PPL) — likely KV cache quant leakage.
2) Instruction-following (few-shot) sensitive to per-channel clipping on a small subset (~0.8% QA drop) which we mitigated by raising clip_range to 8.0 for mix1-int8 in a follow-up run.

eva: How does this affect capacity planning? can we size Dedicated pools with these numbers?

diego: Rough capacity rules of thumb based on throughput: INT8 (H100) ~3x capacity vs FP16, FP8 ~1.7x. So if customer needs 500 rps at p99 latency SLO on FP16 -> for INT8 on H100 you can provision ~1/3 the instance count, but add QA margin for the long-context PPL delta and fallback policy to FP16.
